question: For which English novel was Ruskin Bond honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992?

options.text: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra

solution:
The correct answer is __**Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ruskin Bond was honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 for his English novel **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra".**
 
• The award recognizes and promotes excellence in Indian literature.
 
• **"Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra"** is a collection of short stories that reflect Bond's attachment to Dehradun and his life experiences.
 
• The book is a blend of nostalgia and the author's observations of the changing landscapes and people in Dehra.
 
• Ruskin Bond is renowned for his simple and poignant writing style that captures the essence of rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**:

 
 
• The Sahitya Akademi Award is a literary honour in India, presented annually by the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters.
 
• It recognizes outstanding works of literature in the 24 major Indian languages, including English.
 
• The award includes a plaque and a cash prize.
 
• It is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India, aimed at promoting and preserving Indian literature.
 
 
 
• **Ruskin Bond**:
 
 
• Ruskin Bond is an acclaimed Indian author of British descent, known for his vivid portrayal of life in the Indian hill stations.
 
• He has written numerous novels, short stories, essays, and children's books.
 
• Bond has received several awards for his contribution to literature, including the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.
 
• His works often reflect his deep connection with nature and the simplicity of rural life.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Works by Ruskin Bond**:
 
 
• "The Room on the Roof" – His first novel, which won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.
 
• "The Blue Umbrella" – A beloved children's story that was adapted into a film.
 
• "A Flight of Pigeons" – A novella that was adapted into the film "Junoon".
 
• "Delhi Is Not Far" – A novel that showcases the author's talent for storytelling.
